This document has two purposes. **Work through both before 16 November.**

1. Verify that your R environment works
2. Set up GitHub Copilot for use during the workshop

---

## Part 1: Package installation

Run the chunk below. It installs and loads every package used across the two workshop days. If any package fails, note the error message and reach out before 16 November.

```{r}
#| label: setup
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")

pacman::p_load(
  # Core
  tidyverse,
  haven,
  # Data
  gapminder,
  palmerpenguins,
  carData,
  WDI,
  # Plot extensions
  patchwork,
  ggrepel,
  ggtext,
  ggforce,
  geomtextpath,
  ggridges,
  ggdist,
  waffle,
  # Tables
  kableExtra,
  # Fonts
  showtext,
  sysfonts,
  # Interactive
  ggiraph,
  plotly,
  gganimate,
  dygraphs,
  leaflet,
  # Spatial
  sf
)
```

**Note:** `sf` occasionally requires additional system libraries. If it fails with a message about `GDAL` or `PROJ`, see the [sf installation guide](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/#installing) for your operating system.

## Part 2: Test plot

Render this document (the **Render** button in RStudio, or `quarto render` in the terminal). The plot below should appear in the output. If it does, your environment is ready.

```{r}
#| label: test-plot
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5

gapminder |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = gdpPercap, y = lifeExp,
             size = pop, colour = continent)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar()) +
  scale_size(range = c(2, 12), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Health and wealth across countries (2007)",
    subtitle = "Each point is one country; size = population",
    x = "GDP per capita (log scale)",
    y = "Life expectancy at birth",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

This is a version of the Gapminder chart you analyzed in session 1 (Application 1). Can you identify which variable is mapped to which aesthetic?

## Part 3: GitHub Copilot setup

As a registered student, you have free access to GitHub Copilot through the **GitHub Student Developer Pack**.

### Step 1 — Activate your student access

1. Go to [github.com/education](https://github.com/education) and click **Get student benefits**.
2. Apply with your university email address. Approval is usually instant if your `.edu` address is recognised; otherwise upload a proof of enrolment.
3. Once approved, go to [github.com/settings/copilot](https://github.com/settings/copilot) and enable Copilot for your account (it should show as free under your student plan).

### Step 2 — Enable Copilot in RStudio

Copilot is built into RStudio 2023.09 and later. Update RStudio first if needed ([posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)).

1. *Tools* → *Global Options* → *Copilot*
2. Tick **Enable GitHub Copilot**
3. Click **Sign In** and follow the browser prompt to authorise with your GitHub account

Once enabled, Copilot suggests completions as you type. Accept with **Tab**, dismiss with **Escape**.

### A note on data privacy

Copilot sends the code you are currently editing to GitHub's servers to generate suggestions. **Do not use it when working with restricted-access data** (survey data with a data use agreement, ethics-board-protected data, or anything you are not permitted to share). We will discuss this in the workshop. For ordinary ggplot2 code working with public datasets, it is fine.
